text: Fill in each blank with the correct enzyme, metabolite or clinical feature from the minor carbohydrate pathways.
questions: In hereditary fructose intolerance, deficiency of *aldolase B/Aldolase B* causes accumulation of fructose-1-phosphate in the liver.

Classic galactosaemia is caused by deficiency of *GALT/galactose-1-phosphate uridylyl transferase:The enzyme whose abbreviation shares its first letter with galactose.*, which normally exchanges galactose-1-phosphate with UDP-glucose.
In the polyol pathway, aldose reductase converts glucose to *sorbitol/Sorbitol*, which accumulates in the diabetic lens.
*Galactitol/galactitol* deposited in the lens causes cataracts in galactosaemia.
Hereditary fructose intolerance presents when an infant is weaned onto fruit or sucrose, causing *hypoglycaemia/hypoglycemia* and hepatomegaly.

overallFeedback.feedback: Each inborn error of minor sugar metabolism damages tissues because a metabolite accumulates behind the blocked enzyme — fructose-1-phosphate traps inorganic phosphate causing ATP depletion and hypoglycaemia, while galactitol and sorbitol are osmotically active sugar alcohols that swell the lens and produce cataracts.
